lunch.name: Gravlax (Cured Salmon)
lunch.description: Ancient Scandinavian cured salmon appetizer. Traditionally buried in ground to cure before refrigeration
instructions: Crush peppercorns and coriander seeds
Mix salt, sugar, crushed spices and dill
Rub mixture all over salmon flesh side
Place skin-side down on plastic wrap, wrap tightly
Weight down with cutting board and cans
Refrigerate 3-4 days, turning every 12 hours and discarding liquid
Slice thinly and serve on rye bread with crème fraîche and fresh dill
Pair with mustard sauce
lunch.notes: Daily turning and liquid discarding essential for proper curing. Can be stored refrigerated for 2 weeks
lunch.fun_fact: Gravlax is ancient Scandinavian dish, traditionally buried in ground to cure before refrigeration. Preparation technique unchanged for centuries
alternatives: Serve as appetizer instead of lunch

dinner.name: Swedish Meatballs with Lingonberry Sauce (Traditional Swedish Meatballs)
dinner.description: Traditional Swedish meatballs with creamy gravy - Scandinavian comfort food
instructions: Soak bread in milk for 5 minutes; squeeze out excess
Combine ground beef, pork, soaked bread, grated onion, egg, salt, white pepper, garlic powder, allspice, nutmeg
Mix until just combined; do not overmix
Shape into 20-24 balls
Melt butter in large skillet over medium-high heat
Brown meatballs in batches on all sides (about 12 minutes total); set aside
Reduce heat to medium; sprinkle flour over remaining butter in pan
Whisk constantly for 1-2 minutes to make roux
Gradually add beef stock, whisking constantly
Return meatballs to pan; simmer 5 minutes
Whisk in cream and mustard
Simmer 3-4 minutes; season with salt and pepper
For lingonberry sauce: combine berries, water, lemon juice, lemon zest in pot
Bring to boil; reduce heat and simmer 10-15 minutes until berries soften
Add sugar; stir until dissolved
Serve meatballs with creamy gravy, mashed potatoes, lingonberry sauce on side
dinner.notes: Grated onion instead of minced keeps texture lighter
dinner.fun_fact: Milk-soaked breadcrumbs create tender, bouncy texture
